before: A mobile-first layout starts with a useful narrow arrangement, then adds columns when enough viewport space is available. min-width includes the boundary value and larger widths. This is about available space, not detecting a particular device brand.

The base grid has one flexible column. At 600 CSS pixels or more, the media query replaces it with two equal flexible columns. Keep source order sensible in both arrangements. The preview uses its iframe viewport, not the full app width. A real mobile document also needs the viewport metadata taught in HTML; see the HTML viewport lesson rather than treating CSS as a substitute for that document setting.
Keep one column below 600px and two at or above it, with the same HTML reading order.
after: A responsive layout changes to fit the space available. Mobile-first means you start with a layout that works on a narrow screen.
A media query is a rule that applies only when a condition is met. Here, `min-width: 600px` means the view is at least 600 CSS pixels wide. It includes exactly 600 pixels.
The preview's own width controls this rule. Keep the cards in the same HTML order at both sizes. A real phone page also needs the viewport setting taught in the HTML course.

before.question: At exactly 600px, does (min-width:600px) match?
choices: Yes; the minimum boundary is included.
before.explanation: The min-width condition includes equality. The viewport width is measured in CSS pixels.

after.question: Does min-width: 600px apply at exactly 600 pixels?
after.explanation: Min-width means at least that width, so 600 pixels is included.
